title: PCM's nBlockAlign is the number of bytes of all channels in a frame
summary: nBlockAlign for regular integer PCM = number of channels × bytes per sample container.
detail: A 16-bit two-channel frame occupies 4 bytes; multiply the per-channel sample rate by the frame size to get bytes per second.
boundary: When there is compression encoding, the interpretation of block align varies depending on the encoding and decoding format; the effective number of bits may also be smaller than the number of container bits.
relevance: When splitting stereo samples into left and right channels, avoid mistaking two consecutive samples as adjacent moments of the same channel.
